sections.headline: Tech Stocks Bounce Back
sections.body: The S&P 500 rose 0.53% to 7700.28 as tech stocks rebounded from Friday's selloff, with investors buying into the dip in the AI trade. This move was driven by optimism about the start of the week and the recovery of AI-linked stocks ahead of key earnings. Traders are watching the AI trade closely, as it has been a key driver of market movements in recent days.

sections.headline: Nasdaq Rises on Tech Stocks Optimism
sections.body: The Nasdaq's overnight rise was driven by optimism in the tech sector, with investors buying into AI stocks ahead of key earnings reports. [6] Reuters reported that AI-linked stocks recovered ahead of key earnings, contributing to the Nasdaq's climb. [4] CNBC noted that investors were buying the dip in the AI trade, further fueling the market's upward momentum. [1] [5]

sections.headline: French Protests Boost US Bond Yields
sections.body: Traders are watching the impact of protests in France on the French government's bond yields, which rose on concerns about budget issues. This move is being assessed by investors, causing US Treasury yields to rise as well. The market is also looking at the long-term outlook for US interest rates, with expectations of higher yields for longer, according to some market analysts.

sections.headline: USD/JPY Rises on Yen's Stablecoin Link
sections.body: The USD/JPY pair rose as traders watched the news of Japan's SBI and Singapore's Startale joining the Open Standard to explore a yen-dollar stablecoin link, which may boost the yen's value. [12] This development is seen as a positive catalyst for the yen, as it could increase its use as a reserve currency and stabilize its value. [14] Traders are also keeping an eye on China's Q3 GDP beat, which has led to a rise in the yuan, but the yen's stablecoin link move appears to be the primary driver of the USD/JPY's increase. [11]

sections.headline: Crude Oil Plunges Amid Inflation Concerns
sections.body: Crude oil fell 2.51% to 98.86 as investors became increasingly concerned about inflation, which rose to 3.1% in Canada. This increase in inflation led to a rise in fuel oil prices, making oil less attractive. Traders are watching the Fed's decision on interest rates, which may impact oil prices, for further guidance.

sections.headline: Gold Price Falls Amid Fed Outlook
sections.body: Gold fell 0.5% to 4160.4 as investors weighed the outlook for the Federal Reserve's interest rate decisions, with lower oil prices limiting losses. [16] According to Investing.com, the focus on the Fed rate outlook led to a retreat in gold prices. [20] Meanwhile, Kitco reported that gold ETF holdings reached 2026 highs, bucking the trend of falling prices. [20]

Industry desks:

- Mining: Copper and Silver Rise, Gold Miners Fall. Copper and silver prices are on the rise, driven by strong demand and supply chain constraints, making it a 17-year wait for new mines to come online [26, 27]. The hot inflation trend is putting pressure on gold prices, but investors are taking a different approach by buying gold ETFs, which are hitting 2026 highs [20]. The gap up in Cipher Mining shares suggests that investors are optimistic about the future of mining, but the industry is closely watching for any signs of a downturn [29].
- Timber: Lumber Prices Hit Two-Year Low. Lumber prices have fallen to a two-year low, causing a ripple effect on the timber industry, including a decline in timber stocks like Weyerhaeuser [30, 31]. Industry experts are watching for signs of a potential recovery, as some companies, like Conifex Timber, prepare for a two-shift restart to combat cash crunches and duties [32]. Meanwhile, in the fashion world, Supreme and Timberland are gearing up for a new Fall 2026 collection, which may not be directly related to the timber industry, but could be a distraction for investors [33, 34].
